entries.title: Success
entries.meaning: The sign-in succeeded.
entries.action: Nothing to fix here. If the person still cannot get in, the problem is after sign-in: a licence, an app assignment, or the app itself.

entries.title: Account locked
entries.meaning: Too many wrong passwords, or Microsoft locked the account after seeing a pattern it associates with attackers.
entries.action: If the person was not trying repeatedly, treat it as an attack and look at the source IP before unlocking. Otherwise wait for the lockout to clear or unlock the account in Entra.

entries.title: Password expired
entries.meaning: The password has passed its expiry date.
entries.action: Reset or change the password. Check the password policy if this is a surprise.

entries.title: No password or invalid password
entries.meaning: The sign-in arrived with no password or an unusable one. Common with federation or single sign-on misconfiguration.
entries.action: Check the federation or SSO setup for this user's domain rather than the password itself.

entries.title: Account disabled
entries.meaning: The account is disabled in Entra.
entries.action: If that was not intended, enable it. If it was, the person should not be trying to sign in.

entries.title: Silent sign-in interrupted
entries.meaning: An app tried to sign in without showing anything and Entra needed the person to interact.
entries.action: Usually harmless. The app shows a prompt next and the sign-in completes. Only investigate if it repeats without a successful sign-in after it.

entries.title: MFA registration required
entries.meaning: The person has to register for multifactor authentication before continuing.
entries.action: Have them complete MFA registration. If a registration campaign or policy is new, expect many of these.

entries.title: Strong authentication required
entries.meaning: A policy required a second factor and this sign-in did not provide one yet.
entries.action: Expected once, as the first prompt. If it repeats without a success after it, the person is cancelling the prompt or their method is broken.

entries.title: MFA required again
entries.meaning: Entra asked for a second factor because something changed: a new device, a new location, or an administrator changed MFA settings.
entries.action: Expected after a change. If nothing changed and it keeps happening, look at the device and location on the sign-in.

entries.title: MFA registration required
entries.meaning: The person has to register a multifactor authentication method before this app will let them in.
entries.action: Have them register a method, then sign in again.

entries.title: Device authentication required
entries.meaning: A policy requires a known device and this sign-in came from one Entra does not recognise.
entries.action: Register or join the device, or sign in from a device that already is.

entries.title: Not assigned to the app
entries.meaning: The app requires assignment and this person is not assigned to it.
entries.action: Assign the person, or a group they are in, to the enterprise application.

entries.title: Wrong username or password
entries.meaning: The username or password did not match.
entries.action: Have them try again carefully. Many of these in a short time from one address is a password spray, not a typo.

entries.title: Blocked by Conditional Access
entries.meaning: A Conditional Access policy blocked the sign-in, often a location or device rule.
entries.action: Read the applied policies on this sign-in. The one marked as failed is the reason.

entries.title: Session no longer valid
entries.meaning: The password was changed or reset, which invalidated existing sessions.
entries.action: Sign in again. Nothing to fix unless the change was not expected.

entries.title: Keep me signed in prompt
entries.meaning: The sign-in paused on the stay signed in question.
entries.action: Harmless. The person answers the prompt and continues.

entries.title: On-premises password expired
entries.meaning: The Active Directory password has expired and the sign-in was validated against it.
entries.action: Change the password in Active Directory, then let it sync.

entries.title: Device authentication failed
entries.meaning: The device tried to prove itself to Entra and could not, usually a broken device registration or certificate.
entries.action: Re-register the device, or check its join state in Entra and Intune.

entries.title: External security challenge not satisfied
entries.meaning: A third-party MFA provider or an authentication strength requirement was not met.
entries.action: Check the external MFA integration, or the authentication strength on the policy that applied.

entries.title: Fresh sign-in required
entries.meaning: The token the app held has expired or been revoked and a new sign-in is needed.
entries.action: Sign in again. If sessions are being revoked unexpectedly, check for a sign-in frequency policy.

entries.title: Confirmation needed
entries.meaning: Entra asked the person to confirm the sign-in was really them, for example when switching organizations.
entries.action: Harmless. They confirm and continue.

entries.title: Device not compliant
entries.meaning: A Conditional Access policy requires a compliant device and Intune reports this one as not compliant.
entries.action: Open the device in Intune and see which compliance setting failed. That setting is the fix.

entries.title: Device not domain joined
entries.meaning: A policy requires a Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device and this one is not.
entries.action: Join the device, or sign in from one that is.

entries.title: Device not registered
entries.meaning: A policy requires a registered or managed device and this one is neither.
entries.action: Register or enrol the device, then sign in again.

entries.title: Blocked by Conditional Access
entries.meaning: A Conditional Access policy blocked this sign-in outright.
entries.action: The applied policies on this sign-in name the one that blocked it. Fix the condition or exclude the person, deliberately.

entries.title: MFA registration required
entries.meaning: The person must finish registering for multifactor authentication before this content opens.
entries.action: Have them complete registration.

entries.title: Consent missing
entries.meaning: The app needs permissions this person or organization has not consented to.
entries.action: Grant admin consent for the application, or let the person consent if that is allowed.

entries.title: Session expired
entries.meaning: The refresh token expired, so the app has to sign in again.
entries.action: Sign in again. A short session lifetime policy will cause more of these.

entries.title: Seamless SSO failed
entries.meaning: The Kerberos ticket used for seamless single sign-on was invalid or expired.
entries.action: The next sign-in falls back to a normal prompt. Investigate only if seamless SSO fails for everyone.

entries.title: Account not in this organization
entries.meaning: The account belongs to another organization and has not been invited here.
entries.action: Invite the person as a guest, or have them pick the right organization at sign-in.

entries.title: MFA not completed
entries.meaning: The second factor failed: it timed out, was denied, or the code was wrong.
entries.action: If the person did not start this sign-in, treat it as push bombing and look at the source. Otherwise have them retry with their method ready.

entries.title: Blocked by a security policy
entries.meaning: A Conditional Access policy with a security control, such as an authentication strength or a risk condition, blocked the sign-in.
entries.action: Read the applied policies. If it is risk based, check the person's risk state.

entries.title: Application not found
entries.meaning: The application ID in the request does not exist in this organization.
entries.action: The app is misconfigured or pointed at the wrong tenant. Not a user problem.

entries.title: Public client flow required
entries.meaning: The app sent a request that needs either a client secret or the public client setting on its registration.
entries.action: Enable public client flows on the app registration, or fix the app's authentication code. Not a user problem.
